chapter: Biddle, Durham and early road shows
title: Hippodrome Theater in Danville: Walter Morrow's trio and TOBA shows
summary: He played sideman in a three-piece theater band for touring shows, using arrangements by Eddie Heywood Sr. and backing TOBA acts like the Whitman Sisters.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: So, I didn't know where the boys went. One of the boys went one way, so I got a job playing at the Hippodrome Theater there.
In Danville. So, I played at the Hippodrome Theater for a while.
As the leader or as a side man?
Well, no, a side man band.

The leader was named Walter Morrow. He played piano, and it was three pieces -- drums, piano and trumpet. And we would play all those big shows that come in there. And you know, this Eddie Heywood that wrote this
He had a father who was a piano too.
Well, that's what I'm speaking about.

I met -- fortunately, I met his father. Well, now, his father -- I used to play all his father's arrangements because the shows would come through there and they would have on there, arranged by Eddie Heywood Hayward 81 Theater. He played at the 81 Theater, in Atlanta.
Yes, he was from -- is that the TOBA Circuit?

Toby TOBA Circuit, that's right. T-O-B-A Circuit. That's right. T-O-B-A. We had -- I played Whitman Sisters, I played Sidney Easton and Stewart -- Easton and Stewart and [Denvois]. He had a big troupe -- all those was on that SHW Toby Times, Toby's Time, and they had a circuit that they would play. You're really familiar with that circuit?
I've read a lot about it.
